result.title: Field Emission Enhancement in Graphene/Cu Cathodes Through Laser-Shock-Induced Modulation of Geometry and Work Function.
result.authorString: Xu X, Tao H, Li W, Li X, Lin J, Yang M, Zhou M.
result.abstractText: Cold cathodes enable compact, low-power vacuum microelectronics with rapid activation. Graphene/metal cathodes offer a flexible, conductive platform, but efficient field emission requires local field concentration to coincide with reduced tunneling barriers while avoiding transfer contamination. Laser shock microforming converts graphene/Cu foils into flexible cathodes in one step without transfer while modulating the local work function. High-curvature protrusions and gradients in graphene disorder, strain, Cu microstructure, surface chemistry, and graphene/Cu coupling create spatial variations in the local emission barrier. In individual monolayer graphene/Cu protrusions, these changes produce local work function contrasts reaching 0.12 eV and align lower barriers with highly curved regions. This spatial alignment enhances field emission, yielding a turn-on field of 4.9 V µm<sup>-1</sup>, an emission current density of 2.2 mA cm<sup>-2</sup>, stable emission over 32 h, and durability after 3000 bending cycles. This work extends laser shock processing from geometric shaping to coupled structural and electronic barrier control in graphene/metal cold cathodes, providing a route that can be scaled over large areas for flexible vacuum electronics.

result.title: Improved interfacial-bonding strength and electronic structure properties of graphene-reinforced Al composites by Cu coating.
result.authorString: Jon SH, Ri JB, Jong C, Jong UG, Hong S.
result.abstractText: Cu-coated graphene-reinforced aluminum matrix composites (AMCs) are studied using first-principles calculations. Using Cu-coated graphene, the reinforced AMCs exhibit 1.5 times stronger interfacial bonding than the non-Cu-coated derivative due to hybridization between the 3d orbital of Cu and π orbital of graphene. Our work provides atomic insight into improved interfacial-bonding strength and electronic structure properties of graphene-reinforced AMCs by Cu-coating.
